findings.title: Persisted enum values in `AppendTurnAsync` do not match the schema contract
findings.evidence: Schema: `input_modality IN ('voice', 'text')` and `turn_type IN ('execution', 'clarification', 'confirmation', 'ambiguity_resolution')`. Code: `InputModality = turn.InputModality.ToString(),` and `TurnType = turn.TurnType.ToString(),`
findings.problem: The write path uses raw enum `ToString()` values (`Voice`, `Text`, `Execution`, `Clarification`, `Confirmation`, `AmbiguityResolution`), which do not match the lowercase/snake_case values accepted by the database.
findings.why_it_matters: The core insert path fails as written, or later fixes will change hash inputs and break validation consistency.
findings.proposed_fix: Define explicit enum-to-storage mapping functions for every persisted enum and use them consistently in write code, validators, and hash canonicalization; do not persist raw `ToString()` output.

findings.title: `AppendTurnAsync` can append to a session that has already been closed
findings.evidence: `CloseSessionAsync(sessionId) which sets ended_at = NOW()`. `AppendTurnAsync` reads the tip from `dhf.entries` by `session_id` and inserts new rows, but never checks `dhf.sessions.ended_at`.
findings.problem: A caller with a stale `SessionId` can keep writing entries after the session was closed or superseded.
findings.why_it_matters: This breaks the stated session lifecycle and AddinSessionId epoch semantics; entries can land in a session after the spec says it ended.
findings.proposed_fix: In the append transaction, load the session row `FOR UPDATE` and reject writes when `ended_at IS NOT NULL`; also validate that the caller's expected AddinSessionId matches the session row.

findings.title: The open/resume advisory lock is not scoped to the boundary the method later mutates
findings.evidence: Comment: `Advisory lock to serialize open-or-resume decisions per workstation.` Code: `var lockKey = $"dhf_session_open:{metadata.WorkstationId}:{addinSessionId}";` Later SQL: `UPDATE dhf.sessions SET ended_at = NOW() WHERE ended_at IS NULL AND workstation_id = @WorkstationId`
findings.problem: Different `addinSessionId` values on the same workstation take different locks, but the method then updates all open sessions for that workstation.
findings.why_it_matters: Concurrent opens on one workstation can race, leaving multiple open sessions or closing the wrong session.
findings.proposed_fix: If workstation is the intended concurrency boundary, lock on workstation only. Otherwise, narrow the UPDATE/lookup scope to the same boundary as the lock.

findings.title: The documented unique-violation fallback cannot work as written
findings.evidence: Unique index: `ON dhf.sessions (addin_session_id) WHERE ended_at IS NULL`. Lookup query: `WHERE addin_session_id = @AddinSessionId AND workstation_id = @WorkstationId AND ended_at IS NULL`. Note: `the second will fail on unique-violation and retry via the lookup path.`
findings.problem: No retry logic is specified in the code, and a retry using the documented lookup cannot recover a conflict caused by an open row on another workstation because the lookup filters by workstation.
findings.why_it_matters: Session-open conflicts will surface as raw database failures with undefined recovery behavior.
findings.proposed_fix: Add explicit SQLSTATE `23505` retry handling and make uniqueness, lookup, and retry scopes identical.

findings.title: `dhf.entry_decorations` mutability is specified two different ways
findings.evidence: SDR-04-002: `dhf.entry_decorations is insert-only ... decorations may be superseded by new rows, never mutated in place.` Later: `UPDATE and DELETE are permitted for operational cleanup, so no trigger.`
findings.problem: The spec simultaneously claims decorations are insert-only and allows updates/deletes.
findings.why_it_matters: Consumers cannot know whether decorations are durable audit evidence or disposable operational data.
findings.proposed_fix: Pick one model. If decorations are audit history, enforce insert-only. If cleanup is allowed, define owner, criteria, and how cleanup itself is audited.

findings.title: Viewer-triggered integrity validation is not read-only and has no dedup rule
findings.location: Section 8.2 `Integrity Event Decoration`; Section 9 `DhfRepository`; Section 10.1 `Shallow Validation`
findings.evidence: `Any integrity check failure ... is written as an integrity_event decoration`. `Read-only queries only. No write methods.` `Shallow validation ... runs on every viewer page load.`
findings.problem: A page load can write new rows, and repeated page loads can generate duplicate `integrity_event` decorations for the same defect.
findings.why_it_matters: Read operations mutate the ledger, create unbounded warning spam, and change the dataset under inspection.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep page-load validation side-effect free, or define explicit dedup semantics and move integrity-event writes off the viewer read path.

top_3_must_fix: Align persisted enum serialization with the database CHECK constraints; `AppendTurnAsync` currently writes values the schema rejects.
Reject appends to closed sessions and validate AddinSessionId ownership inside `AppendTurnAsync`.
Repair `OpenOrResumeSessionAsync` so lock scope, lookup scope, uniqueness scope, and conflict-retry behavior are consistent.
